title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: tutorial, re-analyse Crayfish dataset Stern & Crandal (2018)1, re-analysed Bastide et al. (2023)2, available crayfish dataset. dataset contains count RNA-Seq matrix, associated gene lengths, phylogenetic tree crayfish species included study, data-frame specifying whether species blind (0) sighted (1). goal script detect genes significant parallel shift optimum blind species versus sighted species (one hypothesis presented Table Stern & Crandal (2018)3 ).
code: data(crayfish) library(ape) cond_species <- crayfish$sights$sights[match(crayfish$tree$tip.label, crayfish$sights$species)] plot(crayfish$tree, tip.color = hcl.colors(3)[as.numeric(cond_species)])

title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: order apply phyloDE, need normalize data. , use TPM, normalizing factors computed using TMM method.
code: nf <- edgeR::calcNormFactors(crayfish$counts / crayfish$lengths, method = "TMM") #> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes norm_data <- lengthNormalizeRNASeq(crayfish$counts,                                     crayfish$lengths,                                     nf,                                     lengthNormalization = "TPM",                                     dataTransformation = "log2")

title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: construct design matrix, analyse effect sight gene expression.

title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: can plot data heatmap, using phylogenetic structure columns, standard clustering rows.
code: phyHeatmap(norm_data, design, coef = 2, crayfish$tree, margins = c(7, 3))

title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: Finally, apply phylolmFit, syntax similar limma function lmFit. additional argument, takes phylogenetic tree. keep compilation time low, analyse first 500 genes , analysis users use full dataset, parallelize computations using ncores argument.
code: pfit <- phylolmFit(norm_data[1:500, ], design,                    phy = crayfish$tree,                    ncores = 1)

title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: Just limma object, can apply eBayes procedure results. Keep mind analysed first 500 genes, results interpreted directly, plots might look different analyzing full dataset. can check whether trend data plotting mean-variance trend.  apply eBayes, trend. extract significant genes topTable.

title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: standard limma analysis, can perform diagnostic plots. Plot p-values: must uniformly distributed null hypothesis.  MA Plot: points must centered zero, showing biais.  Volcano plot:  Heatmap restricted top 1010 genes:
code: hist(pfit$p.value) plotMD(pfit) abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 3) volcanoplot(pfit, coef = 2, highlight = 10) topGenes <- rownames(topTable(pfit, coef = 2)) phyHeatmap(norm_data[match(topGenes, rownames(norm_data)), ], design, coef = 2, crayfish$tree, margins = c(7, 6))

title: Crayfish Exemple Tutorial
text: diagnostic plots specific phyloDE, fits OU process per gene, regularize parameters (taking trimmed means tanh values). Function getParameters extract regularized parameters. parameters normalized lambda rho values: Values close 0 mean tree little influence (independent errors ). Values close 1 mean tree explains variance (independent errors). Values close 0 mean process looks like BM (selection strength alpha close zero). Values close 1 mean tree close star tree (selection strength alpha large). gene-specific regularized parameters can plotted function plotParameters. Histograms histograms fits genes, dashed lines represent regularized parameters. Modes close 0 1 bounds can expected, especially small parameters.

title: Get Bounds on alpha for an OU — getBoundsSelectionStrength
text: function tries find reasonable bounds \(\alpha\) parameter OU process using scaled phylogenetic half-life \(t_{1/2} = \log(2) / \alpha / h\), \(h\) total height tree. \(t_{1/2} = D)\), means trait need time \(D \times h\) cover half distance optimal value (see Hansen, 1997). Small values \(D\) means high selection pressure (large \(\alpha\)), large values \(D\) means low selection pressure (small \(\alpha\)). default maximum value \(D\) relative_half_life_max = 1e4 (selection week process looks like BM). default minimum value \(D\) relative_half_life_min = 1e-4 (selection strong tips weakly correlated). function makes sure maximum \(\alpha\) value associated relative_half_life_min lead underflow errors rescaling tree.

title: Get Bounds on alpha for an OU — getBoundsSelectionStrength

code: ## Use the normalized Crayfish dataset data(crayfish) # For more details on the normalization, see \code{vignette("crayfish_exemple_tutorial")} norm_data <- lengthNormalizeRNASeq(crayfish$counts, crayfish$lengths)  ## Design matrix design <- model.matrix(~ sights, model.frame(crayfish$sights))  ## Consensus tree (using only genes 1 to 50) ctree <- phylogeneticCorrelations(norm_data[1:50, ], design = design, phy = crayfish$tree) #> Loading required package: ape ctree #> ConsensusTreeModel #>   Consensus tree on: 50 genes. #>   Model: OUfixedRoot, with measurement error. #>   Consensus parameters: lambda = 0.7632214, rho = 0.911506  ## linear model fit using the consensus tree pfit <- phylolmFit(norm_data[1:50, ], design = design, phy = crayfish$tree, consensus_tree = ctree) pfit #> PhyloMArrayLM #>   Fit on: 50 genes. #>   Model:  OUfixedRoot, with measurement error. #>   Using a consensus tree.  ## eBayes correction pfit <- limma::eBayes(pfit, trend = TRUE) limma::topTable(pfit, coef = 2) #>               logFC  AveExpr         t    P.Value adj.P.Val         B #> OG0000013 -1.762035 4.157728 -2.371752 0.02271043 0.3322022 -4.553342 #> OG0000006 -1.123699 4.661495 -2.264746 0.02913447 0.3322022 -4.557420 #> OG0000011 -1.515651 6.119281 -2.198865 0.03385542 0.3322022 -4.559880 #> OG0000045 -1.656621 4.360357 -2.180602 0.03527915 0.3322022 -4.560555 #> OG0000017 -1.246775 3.627495 -2.170592 0.03608178 0.3322022 -4.560923 #> OG0000000 -1.125277 3.112778 -2.125918 0.03986427 0.3322022 -4.562556 #> OG0000041 -1.567679 3.964510 -2.008296 0.05153887 0.3631216 -4.566756 #> OG0000025 -1.957641 4.706274 -1.952082 0.05809945 0.3631216 -4.568710 #> OG0000031 -1.226828 4.569394 -1.849555 0.07192955 0.3996086 -4.572180 #> OG0000046 -0.970511 6.000647 -1.599226 0.11780259 0.5133275 -4.580095  ## title: Phylogenetic Linear Model for Gene Expression Analysis — phylolmFit
text: function performs fit several steps: Fit phylogenetic linear model phylolm gene. use_consensus = TRUE, use trimmed mean transformed parameters get one regularized value genes. step uses phylogeneticCorrelations, similar duplicateCorrelation. details specific parameters used regularization, see function getParameters. Compute estimated phylogenetic correlation matrix \(\hat{C}_g\) gene (genes use_consensus = TRUE). De-correlate normalized data left-multiplying \(\hat{C}^{-1/2}_g\) inverse Cholesky decomposition correlation matrix. Use lmFit de-correlated data. particular, procedure ensures fitted coefficients, stdev.unscaled, sigma df.residual take phylogeny account, can used directly downstream processing eBayes. default bounds phylogenetic parameters phylolm, except alpha parameter OU, use ad-hoc bounds function getBoundsSelectionStrength, sigma2_error intra-specific variance, takes lower bound function getMinError.

title: Phylogenetic Linear Model for Gene Expression Analysis — phylolmFit
code: ## Simulate a tree with tip conditions set.seed(1289) ntips <- 10 tree <- ape::rphylo(ntips, 0.1, 0) condition <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0) plot(tree, tip.color = hcl.colors(3)[condition + 1])   ## Simulate data with 1 to 3 samples per species reps <- sample(1:3, ntips, replace = TRUE) rep_ids <- make.unique(rep(tree$tip.label, times = reps), sep = "_") ngenes <- 20 dat <- matrix(rnorm(sum(reps) * ngenes, 1, 0.5), nrow = ngenes) rownames(dat) <- paste0("g", 1:ngenes) colnames(dat) <- rep_ids  ## Add differentially expressed genes condition_reps <- rep(condition, times = reps) ndiff <- 5 dat[1:ndiff, ] <- dat[1:ndiff, ] + rexp(ndiff, 1/2) %*% t(condition_reps)  ## Design matrix design <- cbind(rep(1, ncol(dat)), condition_reps) colnames(design) <- c("(Intercept)", "condition") rownames(design) <- rep_ids  ## linear model fit pfit <- phylolmFit(dat, design = design, phy = tree) pfit #> PhyloMArrayLM #>   Fit on: 20 genes. #>   Model:  OUfixedRoot, with measurement error. #>   Using a consensus tree.  ## eBayes correction pfit <- limma::eBayes(pfit, trend = TRUE) limma::topTable(pfit, coef = 2) #>          logFC   AveExpr          t      P.Value    adj.P.Val         B #> g2   2.4801330 1.8127645  7.9985315 3.016969e-12 6.033938e-11 17.423416 #> g1   1.6783282 1.3716897  5.7235899 1.209830e-07 1.209830e-06  7.039861 #> g4   1.7538081 1.4047876  5.5060408 3.110442e-07 2.073628e-06  6.121750 #> g5   0.8542889 1.0296559  2.7063159 8.064976e-03 4.032488e-02 -3.525871 #> g13  0.5534069 0.7824108  1.8099043 7.346971e-02 2.522354e-01 -5.448973 #> g15 -0.5651961 0.8212475 -1.7959996 7.567061e-02 2.522354e-01 -5.473288 #> g17 -0.4552155 0.8176752 -1.3476872 1.809613e-01 5.170324e-01 -6.161894 #> g3   0.3247762 1.1046741  1.0831302 2.814896e-01 7.037241e-01 -6.479465 #> g8   0.3384772 0.7251398  1.0044543 3.177090e-01 7.060201e-01 -6.560914 #> g6   0.2393203 0.7514823  0.7978168 4.269648e-01 8.121245e-01 -6.746119  ## title: Compute rho parameter — rhoFromAlpha
text: Function rhoFromAlpha computes rho parameter, defined Cornuault, 2023, Syst. Biol: rho = 1 - (1 - exp(-2 * alpha * t_tree)) / (2 * alpha * t_tree) rho can interpreted percent decrease trait variance caused OU compared variance expected BM. alpha goes 0, rho goes 0: trait can explained "neutral" BM process. alpha goes Inf, rho goes 1: trait exhibits tree structure. Function alphaFromRho computes value alpha value rho. function can expressed using principal Lambert W function. , computed inverting function rhoFromAlpha directly, using function uniroot within alpha_bounds bounds.
